cues.text: Which arterial blood gas result does Guillain-Barré syndrome give?
It is a neuromuscular disease, so the patient cannot ventilate adequately.
Hypoventilation raises carbon dioxide in the blood.
Acute respiratory acidosis occurs with an abrupt failure of ventilation.
A raised PaCO2 decreases the bicarbonate to PaCO2 ratio, and the pH falls.
Other neuromuscular causes include myasthenia gravis and muscular dystrophy.
